analysis: Build per-residue concept labels (31 UniProtKB FT keys) for 5,000 Swiss-Prot proteins from the flat-file FT lines, and a per-concept summary (positive residues, prevalence). Concepts with prevalence >= 1e-3 go forward to SAE-feature scoring (per-residue F1).

error.nature: Bond features are span-filled. In UniProt, 'FT DISULFID i..j' is ONE disulfide bond between Cys i and Cys j (two residues), and 'FT CROSSLNK i..j' is one covalent cross-link between residues i and j. build_label_matrix treats every FT range as a contiguous stretch and labels every residue from i to j. So the DISULFID column marks whole disulfide loops (mostly non-cysteine residues) instead of the bonded cysteines; intrachain CROSSLNK ranges are filled the same way. Single-position records (e.g. interchain bonds) are unaffected.
error.location: code/dataset.py:174 (build_label_matrix: 'labels[s:e, col] = True' is applied to every key, with no case for DISULFID/CROSSLNK, lines 169-174)
error.wrong_result: DISULFID 33,467 positive residues, prevalence 0.02084, rank 5 of 31; SUMMARY.md calls it the largest PTM concept, 'fifth overall', and 'a large and well-populated target'. Only 7.1% of these residues are cysteine (corpus background 1.3%); they form 586 runs of mean length 57.1. CROSSLNK 993 positives (6.2e-4), only 19.0% Lys.
error.correct_result: DISULFID 2,154 positives, prevalence 0.00134, rank 19, just above the 1e-3 floor and close in size to MOD_RES (1,802); 100% cysteine (1,072 i..j records, 2 of them 'i..?' with an unknown partner, plus 29 single-position records: 2,171 bond positions on 2,154 distinct cysteines). CROSSLNK 178 (1.1e-4), 82% Lys. The other 29 columns are identical. The number and set of scored concepts (21) does not change.

detection_rule: Counts as detected if a finding says that DISULFID (or CROSSLNK) FT ranges name two bonded residues (bond ends), not a stretch of sequence, and that the label builder (build_label_matrix / the 'labels[s:e]' range fill) labels the whole range, so these labels cover the loop between the bonded residues and are inflated / mostly not cysteine. Naming this mechanism for either key counts. Not enough: only saying the DISULFID prevalence or rank looks high, or only reporting a low cysteine fraction, without tying it to range-filling of bond records. The finding does not need to give the inflated count or the cysteine fraction; naming the mechanism and the place in the code (build_label_matrix range fill) is enough.
known_true_facts: The label matrix has 1,606,104 rows (= sum of the 5,000 sequence lengths) and 31 columns; rows follow corpus order and prot_index is correct. Row order is not an error.
4,124 of 5,000 proteins carry at least one of the 31 concept keys; the other 876 entries have FT lines only for keys outside the concept list (e.g. CHAIN). This is not an accession-parsing failure.
CA_BIND, METAL and NP_BIND have zero positives because the current UniProt flat-file format folded them into BINDING. This is not a parsing bug.

The FT regex skips qualifier lines (/evidence=, /note=), records whose start is only '?', and records whose position is written on another isoform (e.g. 'P29310-3:149'; these refer to a different sequence, so skipping them is right). Fuzzy bounds like '<12' or '>40' are read as the number, and an unknown end ('1..?') is read as the start position only. In this package this touches 77 of 40,063 concept records (35 skipped: 22 MOD_RES, 9 CONFLICT, 2 MUTAGEN, 1 VARIANT, 1 TRANSIT; 42 read with a fuzzy bound) and changes no conclusion. The fuzzy-bound handling is stated in the parse_features docstring.

Span keys (DOMAIN, REGION, TOPO_DOM, TRANSMEM, HELIX, STRAND, TURN, SIGNAL, TRANSIT, PROPEP, COILED, COMPBIAS, MOTIF, REPEAT, ZN_FING, DNA_BIND, INTRAMEM, ranged BINDING, VARIANT/CONFLICT ranges) really are contiguous stretches, so filling their ranges is right.
CARBOHYD (glycosylation sites, single positions) has 794 positives, 94% Asn, identical in both versions of this analysis.
21 concepts clear the 1e-3 floor in both versions, and it is the same set of 21. ACT_SITE (9.6e-4) and MUTAGEN (6.9e-4) are truly just below the floor.
Prevalence uses all residues (including proteins with no annotation) as the denominator; this is the intended definition.
Sequence positions in the flat file match the corpus sequences (the bonded positions of every DISULFID record are cysteine).
The 5,000 proteins are a uniform random subsample of a uniform sample of Swiss-Prot entries of length 30-1,022.
In this package DISULFID labels are only 7.1% cysteine and form runs of mean length 57 residues (this is the documented error, not a separate issue).

Even with the error, the set of 21 scored concepts is the same as with correct labels; the error changes what the DISULFID concept means (inside a disulfide loop vs bonded cysteine) and its size (15.5x too many positives), not whether it is scored.
The package numbers are exactly the corresponding rows of the original project's full-corpus label matrix (verified bit-for-bit).
possible_false_alarms: Claiming rows of the label matrix are misaligned with the corpus or activations (they are aligned).
Claiming CA_BIND/METAL/NP_BIND being empty shows the parser is broken.
Claiming fuzzy-bound or isoform-position handling ('<', '>', '?', 'P12345-2:...') is a load-bearing error (it touches 77 of 40,063 concept records and does not change any conclusion).
Claiming span-filling is wrong for range features such as DOMAIN, REGION, HELIX, TRANSMEM, SIGNAL, ZN_FING, DNA_BIND or ranged BINDING (these are real stretches).
Claiming the 876 proteins without concept labels reflect missing data or an accession mismatch.

Claiming that treating unannotated residues as negatives (e.g. HELIX/STRAND exist only for proteins with a solved structure) is a load-bearing error in this package. It is a real limitation of using UniProt as ground truth, but it is not an error in label construction; graders should treat it as a caveat, not a detection and not a load-bearing error.
Claiming the 1e-3 floor or the 5,000-protein sample size is an error (they are design choices stated in the README).
Claiming the summary's count of 21 scored concepts is wrong (it matches the outputs).
Claiming that the CROSSLNK error changes which concepts pass the floor (CROSSLNK is below 1e-3 with or without the error: 6.2e-4 vs 1.1e-4).
